analysis: Both changed files are Swift test-only: NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift adds a TextSession fixture and a nativeBlockRequestsCarryNoStopScope test (head lines 50-71, 91-116), and ReasoningStopScopeTests.swift is new (82 lines). No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache storage or coordinator contract is modified in the supplied units. The tests use in-memory fixtures with a fake tokenizer and no network, file or credential access, so they add no new attack surface and do not touch T-041 cache surfaces, TB-002, TB-011 or TB-012. The tests do imply a production behavior change outside this batch: reasoning-scoped stop-string matching (ReasoningStopScope, CBv2StopStringScope, StopHoldback) and the native block engine ignoring the scope. This affects only output truncation semantics (stop sequences inside reasoning or tool-call regions) and the reported matchedStopSequence, not confidentiality or authorization. The production implementation was not supplied. The next pass should check that it cannot let a consumer-supplied stop string suppress or leak reasoning/tool-call content in a way that bypasses output handling, and that the native-block path (which per the test comment matches stops over the whole output) is consistent. These are unverified contracts, not evidenced regressions.
